C.rationale: The proof establishes that two initially white universal vertices preclude any first force, then rules out every set of size at most s. At size s+1 it exhausts the cases with all universal vertices or one white universal vertex and two path vertices, yielding exactly the listed endpoint and adjacent-end-pair sets. Token-jump adjacency gives a clique of size s+1 on each side and one cross-edge. A local C++17 replay checked 261,879 sets over 54 graph instances and verified 1,062 reconfiguration edges; the local copy was not byte-identical to the package source.

evidence: Menon–Singh analyze counts of zero-forcing sets under graph operations; the Resultary bridge-barbell theorem classifies zero-forcing sets of the barbell as the base graph. The fan-graph polynomial result treats s=1, where the reconfiguration graph is a path, not the s≥2 barbell.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These results provide context and nearby boundary cases, but do not imply the all-parameter two-clique-plus-one-bridge reconfiguration graph.

evidence: The proof establishes Z(K_s∨P_n)=s+1, classifies every minimum set, and computes all token-jump adjacencies. Prior work supplies the reconfiguration model and adjacent counting problems, but not this family’s minimum-set classification or unique bridge.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The result is an all-parameter structural realization rather than a corollary of the zero-forcing polynomial of a different base graph.

evidence: Geneson–Haas–Hogben define the token-jumping zero-forcing graph and treat paths, cycles, cliques, disconnected examples and forests. Boyer et al. define the zero-forcing polynomial counting all forcing sets. Neither is the same invariant as the reconfiguration graph of minimum forcing sets for K_s∨P_n.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The target graph is the configuration graph of minimum sets; a zero-forcing polynomial of a barbell base graph is not an equivalent formulation of this reconfiguration claim.
